description: Committee recommends 3% annual funding increases and $100,000 bonus for Discover Saskatoon.
Also recommends $50,000 annual increase to the special events reserve.
Recommends exploring governance reforms for tourism agencies.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Administration believes efficiencies exist in combining agencies, despite Discover's view.
Saskatoon taxpayers may fund increased tourism agency contributions.
Administration could not explain why Saskatoon never ranked first in hotel metrics.
Hotel industry urged stable funding, citing substantial investment in Discover Saskatoon.
Competition Bureau directive impacted Marriott hotels' participation in voluntary funding.
Administration will explore governance reforms for tourism agencies by Q3 2026.

segments.title: Administration presents funding options
description: Report on tourism agency funding and governance.
Discover Saskatoon is an independent non-profit.
City contributes 12-13% of agency's operating revenue.
Recommends performance-based funding structure.

chips.text: $620,000 city core contribution to Discover Saskatoon
Performance-based funding mirrors SREEDA's existing approach

segments.title: Discover Saskatoon chair opposes SREDA amalgamation
description: Discover Saskatoon seeks more funding to do better.
Opposes amalgamation with SREDA; different mandates.
Bid incentive funding is not for Discover Saskatoon operations.

chips.text: Discover Saskatoon chair opposes amalgamation with SREDA
Don't want plastic surgeon doing heart bypass

segments.title: Hotel owners advocate for stable city funding
description: Hotel owners consistently invest in Discover Saskatoon.
Demand generation benefits entire city, not just hotels.
Stable civic investment crucial for long-term sales.

chips.text: Saskatoon hotel owners advocate for stable civic investment
$25.5 million contributed by hotels (2013-2023)

segments.title: Discover Saskatoon CEO on competing for events
description: Saskatoon must actively compete for events and investment.
Visitor economy supports nearly 13,000 jobs.
Special event grants are flow-through, not operating support.

chips.text: $751.9 million in visitor spending last year
Nearly 13,000 people work in the visitor economy

segments.title: Mayor questions bid funding and SREDA synergies
description: Mayor asks about bid funding inclusion in city revenue.
Discusses natural synergies with business attraction.
Asks about Destination Marketing Fee (DMF) changes.

chips.text: Competition bureau directive impacted Marriott hotels' DMF participation

segments.title: Councillor Jeffries questions bid incentive funds
description: Councillor asks about bid incentive funding in other cities.
Ottawa leverages accommodation tax for bid incentives.
Special events reserve is a flow-through fund.

chips.text: $1 million annually from Ottawa's accommodation tax for bid incentives
Discover Saskatoon CEO clarifies funds not under DMO control

segments.title: Councillor Ford questions mandatory hotel tax
description: Councillor acknowledges other tourism economy supporters.
Asks about Destination Marketing Fee (DMF) percentage.
Questions process for mandatory hotel tax via City's Act.

chips.text: Destination Marketing Fee elevated to 4%
Councillor Ford suggests mandatory hotel tax for equal playing field

segments.title: Councillor McDonald questions event bidding environment
description: Councillor asks about event bidding environment post-COVID.
Notes quicker turnaround times, increased event costs.
Questions adequacy of special reserve for large events.

chips.text: Bid fee for World Juniors has doubled since 2020

segments.title: Administration clarifies city funding and hotel tax
description: City's contribution competitive with peer cities.
Mandatory accommodation tax generates significant revenue.
City previously requested province to change City's Act.

chips.text: Ottawa collects $23 million annually from 6% hotel tax
Administration believes mandatory hotel tax is a better solution

segments.title: Administration explores hybrid hotel tax model
description: City investigating a hybrid hotel taxation model.
Model would tax non-participating hotels, refund voluntary ones.
Legal feasibility of approach still under investigation.

chips.text: Legal ability to implement hybrid tax model is uncertain
Hybrid model is a 'plan B' if City's Act isn't changed

segments.title: Administration on SREDA-Discover Saskatoon synergies
description: Administration believes potential governance efficiencies exist.
Compares to SaskTel Centre and TCU Place amalgamation.
City may take direct role in exploring synergies.

chips.text: Administration sees synergies despite organizations' differing views
SaskTel Centre/TCU Place amalgamation cited as example

segments.title: Council votes on governance exploration and agreement
description: Direction to explore governance reforms carried.
Direction to execute 2026-2029 fee-for-service agreement carried.

chips.text: Motion to explore governance reforms and execute agreement carried
Governance discussion to report back by Q3 2026

description: City begins process to amalgamate SaskTel Centre and TCU Place.
Goal is to complete amalgamation by early 2027.
Expected to save $470,000 annually by year three.

chips.text: Approved
Councillor Davies raised concerns about staff having to reapply for all positions.
Employees of SaskTel Centre and TCU Place are affected by potential job changes.
Administration committed to reporting to Council at least twice in 2026 on progress.

description: Committee recommends 3.9% electrical rate increases for 2026, 2027.
Average residential bills would rise $5.61 (2026), $5.85 (2027).
Increases align with SaskPower's proposed rates.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Councillor Dubel questioned interim rates; staff cited increased electricity costs.
Staff promised a new report if the rate panel approves lower increases.
